PullRequest.Title: Keep an agent's required models out of the collapsed Other Models section
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347174

When a custom agent sets `model-policy: required`, the model picker shows only that agent's models. A demoted required model was still sorted into **Other Models**, which starts collapsed. The picker then showed fewer choices than the agent allows, and you had to scroll and expand the section to reach the other one.

Required models are now added to the suggested section, in the agent's order, next to the selected and organization-default models. They are the only valid choices, so none is folded away.

## How I tested

- `ELECTRON_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1 ./scripts/test.sh --grep "Model picker|TabbedModelPicker"` passes, 225 tests. There are two new tests:
  - `buildModelPickerSections`: a demoted required model stays in the shortlist.
  - `TabbedModelPicker`: an agent that requires two models, one demoted, lists both rows and has no Other Models. Without the fix, this test fails.
- `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: clean.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`: passes.
- UI scenario, on Linux, before and after:
  - Setup: an agent requires Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, and the model manifest marks GPT-6.1 Sol as demoted.
  - On Insiders 1.148.0, the picker shows one row and puts GPT-6.1 Sol under a collapsed Other Models.
  - On a dev build of this branch, both rows show.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the model picker for an agent with required models, including a demoted model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatInputPart.getModelsForSessionType already filters the session catalogue to resolved required models; ModelPickerWidget.show passes that pool to TabbedModelPicker._showCurrent. Destination grouping, section construction, item construction and existing ActionList sizing/rendering complete synchronously before the popup is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build the existing virtualized ActionList and measure popup/list geometry
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active list plus an optional sizing build per opening. Each selectable representative appears once; DOM row rendering remains virtualized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same list and sizing machinery ran. _buildItems constructed items for both suggested and other sections before the PR; collapsed demoted items were already represented in memory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous layout/rendering precedes popup interaction. Required demoted rows now participate in the visible list rather than its collapsed section.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P authored preferences and M already-required models, partitioned among provider destinations. The new resolver performs O(P*M_d) in-memory work for a destination with M_d models. Typically a short alternative list, as illustrated by the two-model tests. Existing take() maps and placed set deduplicate identifiers and speed-pair representatives; promotion moves rows rather than duplicating them.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous renderer-thread execution, with an existing optional sizing build and active-tab build. No new asynchronous requests, subprocesses, queues or parallel fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The new resolution has no memoization, but reads supplied metadata rather than discovering models. getModelsControlManifest returns existing state, getLanguageModelGroups reads an existing map, and getVendors filters registered descriptors with cached when clauses. Organization-default derivation is cached per context. A cold/unresolved catalogue does not initiate remote work through the added resolver; the new required-ID array is temporary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the production pool filter, pure preference resolver, destination grouping, map-based deduplication, item construction and virtualized renderer. Existing per-row badge resolution at modelPickerTabbedWidget.ts:1363 is unchanged and already resolves the same agent preferences.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No timing measurements or production preference-list distribution are available. Large authored lists can increase the extra matching scan, but there is no evidenced realistic expensive boundary or independently substantial new work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds a bounded metadata scan per section build and promotes existing required items; it does not increase selectable-model cardinality, eagerly create detail cards, add I/O or retain a growing cache.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enter cross-provider search, switch provider tabs, or refresh an open picker as model/configuration state changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: createActionList builds the active destination's sections, and search builds sections once for each remaining destination before flattening existing items. refresh(models) additionally rebuilds sections for each destination to repopulate speed variants. Ordinary search input filters the existing ActionList and does not invoke _buildSections.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update the existing virtual list and remeasure/layout the popup when sizing changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active-list update per effective refresh, with an optional built-in sizing calculation; deferred detail-page refreshes are coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same destination passes, cross-provider item flattening, sizing calls, updateItems and layout operations already occurred. Search already included pinned, suggested and other models regardless of collapse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing refresh layout runs on the renderer thread. The added pure matching precedes the update only when the consumer rebuilds sections.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P preferences, D nonempty provider destinations, and M required models summed across destinations. One search list build adds O(P*M) matching across disjoint destination catalogues, not D scans of the full catalogue and not per-keystroke resolution. A sizing pass may separately process the built-in subset. Explicit model updates can add another all-destination pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All added matching is synchronous and serialized within list construction. Search input uses existing filtering/cancellation; while a detail page is visible, TabbedActionListWidget coalesces refresh requests into pendingRefresh before rebuilding the list.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Section results and new required-ID arrays are recomputed on explicit list builds. Provider-group and organization-default derivations retain their existing per-context WeakMap caching. Empty matches stay in memory for that call and do not trigger retry, model discovery or network requests. Existing search cancellation and duplicate-input suppression remain unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced _showCurrent.createActionList at 505-517, refresh at 375-427, _buildSearchItems at 1083-1099, and input handling at actionList.ts:1401-1409. The added resolver has no transitive filesystem, database, subprocess, IPC or network operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured matching duration or update-frequency distribution is available; the effective filtered model pool and existing larger per-row matching prevent establishing an actionable additional latency mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Search preserves its item cardinality and does not move preference resolution onto every keystroke. Any unchanged per-row badge matching is outside this PR's scope.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a picker without required-model policy, use added-provider/on-device tabs, or enter model-comparison mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing picker constructs destinations and the requested list. Without required policy, the added conditional skips resolution entirely. With required policy, provider/on-device section builds can perform the same in-memory matching even though only the built-in provider uses suggested sections. Comparison uses the existing active comparison-model context and list refresh path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Zero new preference-matching work without required policy. Otherwise P preferences times the relevant destination catalogue, or the supplied comparison pool partitioned by provider. No duplicate model objects are inserted: take() preserves existing speed-variant collapsing and placed-set deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing synchronous list building and comparison refresh scheduling are unchanged; required-ID resolution neither starts on-device loading nor schedules provider requests. Detail-page refresh coalescing and comparison preserveSize behavior remain intact.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing service metadata and context derivations are reused. No new persistent state, listeners, model cards or cache entries are introduced. Model cards remain obtained through the existing explicit detail/variant paths and are disposed on hide/rebuild; required-ID arrays are not stored on the picker.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the changed mechanism and lifecycle: the resolver uses only metadata arrays, sets and string matching; suggested insertion is guarded by showSuggested; _createModelItem keeps details actions lazy. Existing explicit local-model loadOnSelect and opener actions are unchanged callbacks, not invoked by section construction or promotion.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Comparison catalogues may be larger than the normal required-model pool, and unusual long preference lists are possible. No evidence shows enough newly added work to establish user-visible performance degradation; no durations were measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Non-required workflows add no resolver work. Required-policy provider/comparison workflows add only bounded local scans, without changing expensive boundary counts, concurrency, card lifecycle or retained model cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all four changed files and every diff page against base 1a2bfc8578e7499c836669e490760da715f60b76. Traced production callers, preference matching, grouping/deduplication, list sizing, search input, refresh coalescing and disposal. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression and no concrete performance-regression fix eligible for blame provenance were established. Static review only.
